content.key_idea: A Login application flow is modeled as a small graph of sequential and parallel URL requests, each carrying latency/failure parameters and a backup alternative, from which the simulator derives closed-form duration and failure formulas.
content.reading_order: left to right: Login start into URL1 (with its dashed backup path), then URL2, which fans out into three parallel URLs (3/4/5) that converge at Login end; the parameter legend sits top-right and the two aggregate formulas sit at the bottom

A service is optionally assigned a backup service in case the primary URL fails.

summary: This figure shows how MoCE's simulator models a client application flow, here a 'Login' step, as a small pattern graph of URL requests. Login start leads into URL1 (app.com/token), which has a dashed backup alternative (app.com/backup/token) used if the primary URL fails; the flow continues to URL2 (app.com/info), which fans out into three parallel requests, URL3 (clientinfo), URL4 (init), and URL5 (profile), before converging at Login end. Each URL node carries its own parameters, mean and standard-deviation latency, failure rate, max_retries, and timeout, shown in the top-right legend. Below the graph, two formulas derive the flow's overall behavior from these per-node values: total Login duration sums the sequential URL1/URL2 latencies with the maximum of the three parallel requests, and Login failure is true whenever some request and its backup both fail.
summary_zh: 该图展示MoCE模拟器将"登录"流程建模为URL请求图：URL1有备份URL兜底，URL2后并行发三个请求汇合于结束；每个URL带延迟失败率参数，图下公式据此算总时长与失败概率。
notes: content.groups corrected from the prior label's ['logic'] to ['anatomy']: the figure has no decision diamonds or guarded state transitions (the v3 definition of 'logic'), it is a static request-pattern graph with sequential and parallel edges, annotated below by two aggregate formulas, which matches anatomy's 'worked computation' variant instead.
